describes: Which osv.dev packages each tool the repository pins is published as, so `mise run deps:tools:check` can ask osv.dev for the advisories against each pinned version: one table for the tools `mise.toml` and `mise.lock` pin (`toolPinOsvPackages`), one for the package managers a `packageManager` field names (`packageManagerOsvPackages`), and how long the gate waits for osv.dev's answer (`toolPinQueryTimeoutSeconds`). Each table is keyed by the tool's name as its pin spells it, each row an osv.dev ecosystem and packages, or `unchecked` where osv.dev covers no ecosystem the tool is published in, with the reason for the row in the row.
whyThisFileExists: osv-scanner, which `deps:check` runs, reads neither `mise.lock` nor a `packageManager` field, so no gate saw an advisory against a tool the repository pins (ss-8e9). A tool's name does not say what osv.dev files it under: `gh` is the Go module `github.com/cli/cli/v2`, bd's module is named for the repository it moved from, and Yarn 2 and later are not the npm package `yarn`. That mapping is a decision with a reason, so it is a table keyed by what it governs (`AGENTS.md` § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth), and a record of its own because it binds the toolchain rather than one tool's settings.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run deps:tools:check refuses a pin in `mise.toml` or `mise.lock` with no row in `toolPinOsvPackages`, a `packageManager` with no row in `packageManagerOsvPackages`, a row in `toolPinOsvPackages` that names no pin, a row in either table with neither an ecosystem and packages nor `unchecked` or with both, a row with no `means`, an acceptance without an `until` date and a `reason`, a Go package whose `/vN` suffix does not match the pin's major version, and a `toolPinQueryTimeoutSeconds` that is not a whole number of at least 1. mise run deps:tools:selftest holds each of those refusals over fixture records of its own. No gate holds a row's ecosystem and packages to the tool's real module path or registry name: those were read from each tool's release when the row was written.
whatItDoesNOTDo: It pins no version: `mise.toml`, `mise.lock` and each `packageManager` do. It checks the tool's own packages, and none of what is compiled into it, such as the Go standard library and the Go modules inside `gh`, `bd`, `betterleaks` and `osv-scanner` (ss-b4y). It accepts a finding only in a row's `accepted`, and never through an `osv-scanner.toml`, which only `deps:check` reads.
provenance: Added by ss-8e9 on 2026-11-08, with the gate that reads it. Each row's ecosystem and packages were read that day from the tool's release: the `module` line of its `go.mod` at the pinned tag for a Go program, and the registry it is published to otherwise. Each row's figures are osv.dev's answers to a query that day. The review of ss-8e9 the same day moved each row's package into a list, added bd's second module path, the package-manager table and the timeout.

betterleaks.means: Betterleaks is a Go program, and `go.mod` at tag v1.9.0 declares the module `github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks`. GitHub files a Go project's advisories under its module path. osv.dev listed none against 1.0.0 or 1.9.0 on 2026-11-08, so the row is held only by the Go ecosystem's coverage. Where it loses: an advisory filed under another module path passes.

gh.means: gh is a Go program, and `go.mod` at tag v2.102.0 declares the module `github.com/cli/cli/v2`. osv.dev listed 16 advisories against 2.20.0 and none against 2.102.0 on 2026-11-08. Where it loses: an advisory filed only under the pre-v2 path `github.com/cli/cli` passes.

github:gastownhall/beads.means: bd is a Go program, and `go.mod` at tag v1.3.0 declares the module `github.com/steveyegge/beads`, named for the repository it moved from. The gate also asks `github.com/gastownhall/beads`, the repository's own path, where an advisory filed against the repository would land. osv.dev listed none against 0.1.0 or 1.3.0 under the first path, and none against 1.3.0 under the second, on 2026-11-08, so asking both costs no false finding today. Where it loses: a later tag that renames the module needs this row moved with the pin.

node.means: osv.dev has no ecosystem for Node.js itself. It imports Bitnami's vulnerability database as the `Bitnami` ecosystem, which files Node.js's own advisories under `node`, against upstream version numbers. On 2026-11-08 it listed 81 advisories against 20.0.0, 8 against 24.21.0 and none against 24.22.1. osv-scanner 2.6.0 matched none of them, which is why the gate asks osv.dev's API itself. Where it loses: an advisory Bitnami has not imported yet passes, and if Bitnami stops filing `node`, every version reads as clean.

npm:pnpm.means: mise installs pnpm from npm, where it is published as `pnpm`. osv.dev listed 17 advisories against 11.1.2 and none against 11.28.8 on 2026-11-08.

osv-scanner.means: osv-scanner is a Go program, and `go.mod` at tag v2.6.0 declares the module `github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2`. osv.dev listed none against 2.0.0 or 2.6.0 on 2026-11-08, so the row is held only by the Go ecosystem's coverage.

uv.means: uv is published to PyPI as `uv`, and its advisories are filed there. osv.dev listed 9 advisories against 0.5.0 and none against 0.13.5 on 2026-11-08. Where it loses: an advisory filed only against uv's Rust crates passes.

toolPinOsvPackagesMeans: The osv.dev packages each mise tool is checked as, keyed by the tool's name in `mise.toml` and `mise.lock`. A row is `ecosystem` and `packages`, osv.dev's names for where the tool is published, each package asked for the pinned version; or it is `unchecked: true`, where osv.dev covers no ecosystem the tool is published in, which the gate prints as unchecked on every run. Every row says why in `means`. A row may add `accepted`, keyed by advisory id, each with an `until` date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and a `reason`; the gate passes that advisory through that date, and fails on it after. A tool added to `mise.toml` adds its row in the same change, or the gate refuses it; a tool removed takes its row with it. A Go package's `/vN` suffix moves with the pin's major version, or the gate refuses it. Where it loses: a row with the wrong package checks a package the tool is not, and passes, because osv.dev answers a query for any name.

npm.means: corepack fetches npm from the npm registry, where it is published as `npm`. osv.dev listed 4 advisories against 6.0.0 on 2026-11-08. No `package.json` here names npm as its `packageManager` yet; the row is here so that one would be checked, not printed as unchecked.

pnpm.means: corepack fetches pnpm from the npm registry, where it is published as `pnpm`, the package `npm:pnpm` in `toolPinOsvPackages` names too. `src/package.json` names `pnpm@11.28.8`.

packageManagerOsvPackagesMeans: The osv.dev packages each package manager a `packageManager` field names is checked as, keyed by the name before its `@`, in the same row shape as `toolPinOsvPackages`. A name no row maps is refused, as a mise pin with no row is, and the refusal names this table and this record; the operator chose that on 2026-11-08 (ss-8e9). A name is mapped only once someone has read where it is published, because the name is not always the package: Yarn 2 and later publish as `@yarnpkg/cli-dist` rather than `yarn`. A row with no `package.json` naming it is not refused, unlike a row in `toolPinOsvPackages`. Where it loses: a project that moves to a package manager with no row fails every push until someone adds the row.
toolPinQueryTimeoutSecondsMeans: How long `scripts/check-tool-pins.mjs` waits for osv.dev's one batch answer before it fails the gate as unchecked, instead of holding a push or a CI job. The gate's one real run on 2026-11-08 took 0.45 s end to end through `mise run`, so 30 s leaves room for a slow network without making an outage cost more than half a minute. The selftest's fixtures set 2. Where it loses: an osv.dev slower than this fails every push and every pull request until it recovers, where a longer wait would have passed.
